newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina legislature advances stock tax refunds.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina legislature advances stock tax refunds.

text.p: Finance committees in North Carolina's House and Senate have approved a proposal to refund $156 million to residents who paid the state's intangibles tax on investments under protest, the Journal said Wednesday.

The U.S. Supreme Court struck down the tax last year, ruling that it violated interstate commerce laws because the stock of in-state companies was taxed at a lower rate than that issued by out-of-state companies.
The state gave discounts based on the percentage of the firm's business that was conducted in North Carolina.
But the court left it up to the General Assembly to decide whether to issue refunds to those who paid under protest, or seek retroactive payments from those who used the discounts.
Proposals approved in the House and Senate finance committees would pay refunds to about 142,000 taxpayers who paid the disputed tax under protest for tax years 1990 through 1994.
The state attorney general previously ruled the state couldn't issue refunds to another 231,000 taxpayers who failed to file a protest within 30 days of paying the disputed tax.
